draft.title: Static and dynamic equilibrium
card: Some reactions are reversible: the products can react to re-form the reactants. The forward reaction makes products. The reverse reaction makes reactants.
the forward and reverse reactions both continue at the same rate. The amounts of reactants and products stay constant, but particles are still reacting.
nothing is changing at the particle level. No reaction is going on in either direction, so the amounts stay constant.
Chemical equilibrium is dynamic. It needs a closed system, where no matter enters or leaves. In an open container, a gas product can escape and equilibrium is not reached.
draft.remember: At equilibrium the amounts are constant because both reactions run at equal rates, not because they have stopped.

a.q: A reversible reaction in a sealed flask has reached equilibrium. Which statement about the flask is correct?
opts: The forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates
The forward reaction goes on but the reverse has stopped
Both reactions have stopped, so the amounts are constant
The amounts of reactants and products are always equal
a.why: At equilibrium both reactions continue, and equal rates keep the amounts constant. Saying both reactions have stopped describes static equilibrium, which is not how chemical equilibrium works. Constant amounts do not have to be equal amounts.
a.clue: Constant amounts do not mean that nothing is happening.

b.q: Dani places some solid calcium carbonate in an open dish and heats it. It breaks down into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide gas, and the gas escapes into the room. Why does this system not reach equilibrium?
opts: It is an open system, so the product gas leaves
The reverse reaction is not possible for this change
The forward reaction stops once the dish is heated
The amounts of solids cannot stay constant in a dish
b.why: Equilibrium needs a closed system. Carbon dioxide escapes, so it cannot react with calcium oxide to re-form calcium carbonate at the same rate as the forward reaction. The reaction is reversible in a sealed container, so the reverse reaction being impossible is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what happens to the gas in an open dish.

a.best: The forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates

b.best: It is an open system, so the product gas leaves
